svg.title: Mist makes the familiar forest difficult to recognize.

text.tspan: Mist makes the familiar forest difficult to recognize.
uncanny
US /ʌnˈkæni/ adjective
uncanny · more uncanny · most uncanny; noun: uncanniness
Strange and difficult to explain, often in a way that makes you feel
uneasy.
eerie; strangely unsettling · Eerie emphasizes unease; uncanny can
also describe a startling resemblance or ability.
In the fog, the familiar path had an uncanny stillness, as if the whole
forest were holding its breath.
Use uncanny before a noun or after seem, feel or look. An uncanny
resemblance is strikingly exact; it need not be frightening.
A: This is the path we walked yesterday, isn’t it?
B: Yes, but the fog makes it feel uncanny. I can barely see the next
tree.
A: And there’s not a sound. Shall we head back?
B: Let’s. I’d rather take the road while it’s still light.
Choose the more natural use of uncanny and explain why: (a) The
twins, who had never met, used exactly the same unusual
expressions. (b) The bus arrived at its advertised time. (Model: (a).
Their unexpectedly exact similarity is difficult to explain. A bus arriving
on schedule is ordinary, so uncanny would usually be inappropriate.)
